slides.headline: Similarity criteria
slides.sub: AA (or AAA) · SSS · SAS — any one proves two triangles are similar

slides.headline: Basic Proportionality Theorem
slides.sub: A line parallel to one side divides the other two sides in the same ratio (Thales).

slides.headline: Ratio of areas
slides.sub: Areas of two similar triangles are in the ratio of the SQUARES of corresponding sides.

slides.headline: Pythagoras theorem
slides.sub: In a right triangle: hypotenuse² = base² + perpendicular²

subject: Maths
cover: Circle theorems that solve every problem

slides.headline: Tangent ⟂ radius
slides.sub: A tangent is perpendicular to the radius at the point of contact.

slides.headline: Equal tangents
slides.sub: The lengths of two tangents drawn from an external point are equal.

slides.headline: Tangent length
slides.sub: Length of tangent = √(d² − r²), where d = distance of point from centre, r = radius.

slides.headline: Circle basics
slides.sub: Area = πr² · Circumference = 2πr

slides.headline: Area of a sector
slides.sub: Area of sector = (θ/360) × πr², where θ = angle of the sector

slides.headline: Length of an arc
slides.sub: Arc length = (θ/360) × 2πr

slides.headline: Area of a segment
slides.sub: Area of segment = area of sector − area of the triangle formed

subject: Maths
cover: Heights & Distances: how to set it up

slides.headline: Angle of elevation
slides.sub: The angle UP from the horizontal to an object above you.

slides.headline: Angle of depression
slides.sub: The angle DOWN from the horizontal to an object below you.

slides.headline: The key relation
slides.sub: Use tan θ = height / horizontal distance (draw the right triangle first).

subject: Chemistry
cover: Metals vs Non-metals: what to remember

slides.headline: Reactivity series
slides.sub: K > Na > Ca > Mg > Al > Zn > Fe > Pb > (H) > Cu > Ag > Au (most → least reactive)

slides.headline: Ionic compounds
slides.sub: Formed by transfer of electrons (metal + non-metal); high melting points; conduct when molten.

slides.headline: Corrosion
slides.sub: Metals react with air/moisture (e.g., iron rusts). Prevented by painting, galvanising, alloying.

slides.headline: Alloys
slides.sub: A mixture of a metal with other elements (e.g., steel, brass) — often stronger / rust-resistant.

slides.headline: Modern periodic law
slides.sub: Properties of elements are a periodic function of their ATOMIC NUMBER.

slides.headline: Structure
slides.sub: 18 vertical groups · 7 horizontal periods

slides.headline: Across a period (→)
slides.sub: Atomic size decreases · metallic character decreases · non-metallic character increases

slides.headline: Down a group (↓)
slides.sub: Atomic size increases · metallic character increases

slides.headline: Right-hand thumb rule
slides.sub: Thumb points along the current; curled fingers show the direction of the magnetic field.

slides.headline: Fleming's left-hand rule
slides.sub: Force on a current-carrying conductor in a field: Thumb = force, Forefinger = field, Middle = current.

slides.headline: Fleming's right-hand rule
slides.sub: Direction of induced current in a generator (electromagnetic induction).

slides.headline: Solenoid
slides.sub: A coil of wire acts like a bar magnet when current flows; field inside is uniform.
